reuse.why: Reuses recurrence construction and weekend adjustment helpers, but the handlers independently implement the daily skip-versus-move policy.

duplication.why: Daily occurrence filtering is repeated across shared and handler code, and budget calculation retains two parallel adjustment blocks.

placement.why: Holiday recognition belongs in shared schedules, but occurrence policy remains spread across shared utilities, server handlers, and budget calculation.

scope.why: The edits consistently address the four requested schedule changes and their tests, types, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The small holiday helpers are understandable, but duplicated occurrence policy and independently chosen scan bounds make future changes harder to coordinate.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange independently filter daily occurrences rather than sharing the filtering introduced in firstWeekdayOccurrence; createScheduleList continues to bypass getNextDate adjustment and apply it locally.

disguised_duplication.where: firstWeekdayOccurrence returns an accepted occurrence, getUpcomingDates conditionally pushes it, and getDatesInRange continues past rejected occurrences, reshaping the same daily weekend/holiday filtering decision.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; getNextDate gains daily-specific forward and reverse selection branches; two handler loops and two budget adjustment sites independently orchestrate occurrence policy.
